chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'In how much is the thief's hand cut?' He said, 'In a quarter of a Dinar.' I said to him, 'In two Dirhams?' He said, 'In a quarter of a Dinar, [the value of] the Dinar reaching what it reaches.'

He (the narrator) said, 'So I said to him, 'What is your view of the one who steals less than a quarter of a Dinar? Does the name of the thief befall him, and is he a thief in the Presence of Allah in that state?' He said, 'Every one who steals anything from a Muslim, so he has taken it and secured it in his possession, upon him befalls the name of the thief, and he is a thief in the Presence of Allah. But, his hand is not cut except in a quarter of a Dinar or more. And if the hands of the thieves were to be cut regarding what is less than a quarter of a Dinar, you would find the generality of the people as being (hand) cut.'

key_terms.رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ: Quarter of a Dinar (minimum value for hadd punishment)
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: To be cut (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of goods required for a thief's hand to be cut according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the ontological state of being a 'thief' (sariq) before Allah, which applies to any theft of appropriated goods, and the juridical application of hadd punishment, which is restricted to a minimum value of one-quarter of a Dinar. This threshold ensures that the severe physical penalty is not applied to minor infractions, thereby preventing the general populace from being disproportionately punished for small thefts. The narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing strict legal definitions with practical justice and mercy.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Regarding how much would the thief’s (hand) be cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a quarter of a Dinaar’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Regarding to Dirhams?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a quarter of a Dinar, the (value of the) Dinar reaching what it reaches’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of the one who steals less than a quarter of a Dinar when he steals, he would be named as a thief, and is he a thief in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in that state?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every one who steals anything from a Muslim, so he has taken it and kept it in his possession, so upon him would occur the name of the thief, and he would be a thief in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, but, his hand would not be cut except with regards to a quarter of a Dinar, or more. And if the hands of the thief were to be cut regarding what is less than a quarter of a Dinaar, you would find the generality of the people as being (hand) cut’.
